chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of agricultural, forestry, aquacultural, and related workers.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Assign tasks such as feeding and treatment of animals, and cleaning and maintenance of animal quarters.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Record the numbers and types of fish or shellfish reared, harvested, released, sold, and shipped.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Monitor workers to ensure that safety regulations are followed, warning or disciplining those who violate safety regulations.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Observe animals for signs of illness, injury, or unusual behavior, notifying veterinarians or managers as warranted.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Observe fish and beds or ponds to detect diseases, monitor fish growth, determine quality of fish, or determine completeness of harvesting.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Train workers in tree felling or bucking, operation of tractors or loading machines, yarding or loading techniques, or safety regulations.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Treat animal illnesses or injuries, following experience or instructions of veterinarians.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Train workers in spawning, rearing, cultivating, and harvesting methods, and in the use of equipment.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Train workers in techniques such as planting, harvesting, weeding, or insect identification and in the use of safety measures.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Confer with managers to evaluate weather or soil conditions, to develop plans or procedures, or to discuss issues such as changes in fertilizers, herbicides, or cultivating techniques.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Communicate with forestry personnel regarding forest harvesting or forest management plans, procedures, or schedules.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Inspect crops, fields, or plant stock to determine conditions and need for cultivating, spraying, weeding, or harvesting.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Coordinate dismantling, moving, and setting up equipment at new work sites.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Coordinate the selection and movement of logs from storage areas, according to transportation schedules or production requirements.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Schedule work crews, equipment, or transportation for several different work locations.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Drive or operate farm machinery, such as trucks, tractors, or self-propelled harvesters, to transport workers or supplies or to cultivate or harvest fields.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Perform both supervisory and management functions, such as accounting, marketing, and personnel work.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Transport or arrange for transport of animals, equipment, food, animal feed, and other supplies to and from work sites.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Inspect buildings, fences, fields or ranges, supplies, and equipment to determine work to be performed.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Read inventory records, customer orders, or shipping schedules to determine required activities.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Inspect facilities to determine maintenance needs.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Confer with managers to determine production requirements, conditions of equipment and supplies, and work schedules.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Prepare and maintain time or payroll reports, as well as details of personnel actions, such as performance evaluations, hires, promotions, or disciplinary actions.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Requisition or purchase supplies, such as insecticides, machine parts or lubricants, or tools.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Monitor or oversee construction projects, such as horticultural buildings or irrigation systems.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Issue equipment, such as farm implements, machinery, ladders, or containers to workers, and collect equipment when work is complete.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Calculate or monitor budgets for maintenance or development of collections, grounds, or infrastructure.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Direct or assist with the adjustment or repair of equipment or machinery.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Monitor operations to identify and solve problems, improve work methods, and ensure compliance with safety, company, and government regulations.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Plan work schedules according to personnel and equipment availability.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Assign duties or work schedules to employees.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Record agricultural or forestry inventory data.

chunks.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
chunks.text: Inspect products or operations to ensure that standards are met.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Inspect agricultural commodities, processing equipment, and facilities, and fish and logging operations, to ensure compliance with regulations and laws governing health, quality, and safety.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Inspect food products and processing procedures to determine whether products are safe to eat.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Interpret and enforce government acts and regulations and explain required standards to agricultural workers.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Inspect agricultural commodities or related operations, as well as fish or logging operations, for compliance with laws and regulations governing health, quality, and safety.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Label and seal graded products and issue official grading certificates.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Monitor the operations and sanitary conditions of slaughtering or meat processing plants.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Take emergency actions, such as closing production facilities, if product safety is compromised.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Verify that transportation and handling procedures meet regulatory requirements.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Inspect the cleanliness and practices of establishment employees.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Examine, weigh, and measure commodities, such as poultry, eggs, meat, or seafood to certify qualities, grades, and weights.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Inspect or test horticultural products or livestock to detect harmful diseases, chemical residues, or infestations and to determine the quality of products or animals.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Monitor the grading performed by company employees to verify conformance to standards.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Write reports of findings and recommendations and advise farmers, growers, or processors of corrective action to be taken.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Collect samples from animals, plants, or products and route them to laboratories for microbiological assessment, ingredient verification, or other testing.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Provide consultative services in areas such as equipment or product evaluation, plant construction or layout, or food safety systems.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Compare product recipes with government-approved formulas or recipes to determine acceptability.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Inspect products or operations to ensure that standards are met.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Examine animals to detect illness, injury or other problems.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Advise others on farming or forestry operations, regulations, or equipment.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Warn individuals about rule violations or safety concerns.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Mark agricultural or forestry products for identification.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Package agricultural products for shipment or further processing.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Measure physical characteristics of forestry or agricultural products.

chunks.title: Agricultural Inspectors
chunks.text: Testify at legal or legislative proceedings.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Select and breed animals according to their genealogy, characteristics, and offspring. May require knowledge of artificial insemination techniques and equipment use. May involve keeping records on heats, birth intervals, or pedigree.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Feed and water animals, and clean and disinfect pens, cages, yards, and hutches.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Observe animals in heat to detect approach of estrus and exercise animals to induce or hasten estrus, if necessary.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Treat minor injuries and ailments and contact veterinarians to obtain treatment for animals with serious illnesses or injuries.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Purchase and stock supplies of feed and medicines.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Select animals to be bred, and semen specimens to be used, according to knowledge of animals, genealogies, traits, and desired offspring characteristics.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Examine animals to detect symptoms of illness or injury.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Build hutches, pens, and fenced yards.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Record animal characteristics such as weights, growth patterns, and diets.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Brand, tattoo, or tag animals to allow animal identification.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Arrange for sale of animals and eggs to hospitals, research centers, pet shops, and food processing plants.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Place vaccines in drinking water, inject vaccines, or dust air with vaccine powder to protect animals from diseases.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Exercise animals to keep them in healthy condition.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Adjust controls to maintain specific building temperatures required for animals' health and safety.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Maintain logs of semen specimens used and animals bred.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Inject prepared animal semen into female animals for breeding purposes, by inserting nozzle of syringe into vagina and depressing syringe plunger.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Clip or shear hair on animals.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Package and label semen to be used for artificial insemination, recording information such as the date, source, quality, and concentration.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Measure specified amounts of semen into calibrated syringes, and insert syringes into inseminating guns.

chunks.title: Animal Breeders
chunks.text: Examine semen microscopically to assess and record density and motility of gametes, and dilute semen with prescribed diluents, according to formulas.

chunks.text: Load and unload crops or containers of materials, manually or using conveyors, handtrucks, forklifts, or transfer augers.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Mix specified materials or chemicals, and dump solutions, powders, or seeds into planter or sprayer machinery.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Spray fertilizer or pesticide solutions to control insects, fungus and weed growth, and diseases, using hand sprayers.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Observe and listen to machinery operation to detect equipment malfunctions.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Manipulate controls to set, activate, and adjust mechanisms on machinery.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Operate or tend equipment used in agricultural production, such as tractors, combines, and irrigation equipment.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Adjust, repair, and service farm machinery and notify supervisors when machinery malfunctions.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Attach farm implements such as plows, discs, sprayers, or harvesters to tractors, using bolts and hand tools.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Load hoppers, containers, or conveyors to feed machines with products, using forklifts, transfer augers, suction gates, shovels, or pitchforks.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Direct and monitor the activities of work crews engaged in planting, weeding, or harvesting activities.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Operate towed machines such as seed drills or manure spreaders to plant, fertilize, dust, and spray crops.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Weigh crop-filled containers, and record weights and other identifying information.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Walk beside or ride on planting machines while inserting plants in planter mechanisms at specified intervals.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Drive trucks to haul crops, supplies, tools, or farm workers.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Guide products on conveyors to regulate flow through machines, and to discard diseased or rotten products.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Position boxes or attach bags at discharge ends of machinery to catch products, removing and closing full containers.

chunks.title: Agricultural Equipment Operators
chunks.text: Irrigate soil, using portable pipes or ditch systems, and maintain ditches or pipes and pumps.

chunks.text: Sell and deliver plants and flowers to customers.

chunks.title: Fishing and Hunting Workers
chunks.text: Hunt, trap, catch, or gather wild animals or aquatic animals and plants. May use nets, traps, or other equipment. May haul catch onto ship or other vessel.

chunks.text: Stop saw engines, pull cutting bars from cuts, and run to safety as tree falls.

chunks.title: Fallers
chunks.text: Saw back-cuts, leaving sufficient sound wood to control direction of fall.

chunks.title: Fallers

chunks.title: Fallers
chunks.text: Determine position, direction, and depth of cuts to be made, and placement of wedges or jacks.

chunks.title: Fallers
chunks.text: Control the direction of a tree's fall by scoring cutting lines with axes, sawing undercuts along scored lines with chainsaws, knocking slabs from cuts with single-bit axes, and driving wedges.

chunks.title: Fallers
chunks.text: Trim off the tops and limbs of trees, using chainsaws, delimbers, or axes.
